mnemonic: 나머지 = the remainder: so much feeling that the overflow spills into an action.
meaning: so … that (as a result of too much …), usually with an unintended outcome
nuance: An excess of some feeling or state (긴장, 당황, 흥분, 서두르다, 기쁘다) leads to a result the person usually didn't intend: 당황한 나머지 엉뚱한 대답을 했다. Both verbs and adjectives take -(으)ㄴ. The main clause reports what happened, so it can't be a command or suggestion. Slightly formal and common in narrative writing and news, but perfectly usable in speech.

contrasts.note: -다 못해 is about reaching a limit (참다못해, 'unable to hold back any longer') or spilling past one degree into another (짜다 못해 쓰다).
-(으)ㄹ 지경이다 describes being on the verge of an extreme state, not an action that resulted.

mnemonic: 못해 = 'couldn't (go on)': you tried to keep going, and you couldn't.
meaning: (V) unable to keep … up any longer, finally …; (A) so … that it goes beyond into …
nuance: Two uses. With verbs of enduring or watching (참다, 견디다, 보다, 기다리다), the person held out as long as they could and then acted: 보다못해 한마디 했다 ('unable to stand by any longer'). With adjectives, a quality is pushed past its limit into a further, more extreme state: 하얗다 못해 창백하다, 지루하다 못해 졸리다. 참다못해 and 보다못해 are adverbs in 표준국어대사전 and are written closed up; elsewhere keep the space (기다리다 못해, 지루하다 못해).

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ 나머지 is an excess of feeling causing an (unintended) action; -다 못해 is a limit of endurance reached.
-(으)ㄹ 지경이다 is the verge of an extreme; -다 못해 has already crossed into it.

mnemonic: 地境 = a border: you're standing right at the border of losing it.
meaning: to the point of …; on the verge of … (an extreme, usually bad state)
nuance: Hyperbolic degree: things have gotten so bad that someone is on the verge of an extreme state (미칠 지경이다, 쓰러질 지경이다, 숨이 막힐 지경이다). Usually negative and often exaggerated for effect. The more formal frame is -(으)ㄹ 지경에 이르다 ('reach the point of'). 지경 (地境) is literally a boundary.

contrasts.note: -다 못해 has already crossed the line into the next state; -(으)ㄹ 지경이다 is right at the edge.

mnemonic: 버리다 = throw away: the action is done and tossed behind you, for better or worse.
meaning: (do something) completely; end up … (with relief, regret, or decisiveness)
nuance: Marks an action as done and gone, colored by the speaker's feeling about it: regret (지갑을 잃어버렸다), relief at being rid of something (밀린 일을 다 끝내 버렸다), or brisk decisiveness (그냥 말해 버려). It is common in commands and suggestions (빨리 끝내 버리자) and very frequent in speech. As an auxiliary it may be spaced or attached (먹어 버리다 / 먹어버리다), and some compounds are single dictionary words (잊어버리다, 잃어버리다).

contrasts.note: -고 말다 stresses an outcome reached despite resistance (often regrettable) or a firm resolve; it isn't used for breezy commands or suggestions, where -아/어 버리다 is natural.

mnemonic: 말다 = stop: the story stops at this ending, whether you wanted it or not.

cloze.sentence: 아기가 밤새 보채는 바람에 {{}} 하고 출근했다.
cloze.en: The baby fussed all night, so I barely slept before heading to work.

nearMiss.hint: -다시피 하다 would mean you practically slept the whole time, the opposite of what happened.

cloze.sentence: 아들은 게임에 빠져서 내 말에 {{}} 했다.
cloze.en: My son was so absorbed in his game that he barely answered me.

cloze.sentence: 너무 피곤해서 {{}} 하고 바로 잠들었어요.
cloze.en: I was so tired that I barely washed before falling asleep.

cloze.sentence: 설거지한 그릇을 {{}} 해서 물기가 그대로 남아 있었다.
cloze.en: He barely dried the washed dishes, so they were still dripping.

cloze.sentence: 선배는 내 설명을 {{}} 하더니 자기 할 말만 했다.
cloze.en: My senior barely listened to my explanation before launching into what he wanted to say.

nearMiss.hint: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 들은 둥 만 둥.

nuance.situation: 동료가 실수를 하고 사과를 하긴 했는데, 건성으로 대충 하고 넘어갔어요. (Your colleague did apologize, but only perfunctorily.)

options.text: 그 사람은 사과를 하는 둥 마는 둥 하고 넘어갔다.
options.why: -는 둥 마는 둥: he did apologize, but so half-heartedly it barely counted.

options.text: 그 사람은 사과를 하기는커녕 오히려 화를 냈다.
options.why: -기는커녕 says he didn't apologize at all, which contradicts the situation.

options.text: 그 사람은 사과를 하다시피 하고 넘어갔다.
options.why: -다시피 하다 means 'practically (fully) did', which overstates a perfunctory apology.

nuance.situation: 시험 전날 밤 걱정 때문에 잠을 거의 못 잤어요. 친구에게 말하려면? (You hardly slept the night before the exam because of nerves. You tell a friend.)

options.text: 걱정 때문에 자는 둥 마는 둥 했어.
options.why: -는 둥 마는 둥: you slept, but so fitfully it barely counted.

options.text: 걱정 때문에 자다시피 했어.
options.why: -다시피 하다 means you practically did sleep all the way, which is the opposite.

options.text: 걱정 때문에 자기는커녕 푹 잤어.
options.why: -기는커녕 denies sleeping and then says you slept soundly, a contradiction.

mnemonic: -느니 points at the option you're throwing out; 차라리 picks up the one you'll grudgingly keep.
nuance: Both options are bad; the speaker rejects the one marked with -느니 and picks the other as the lesser evil. Verbs only (plus 있다/없다). The main clause typically ends in -는 게 낫다, -겠다, or a suggestion, and 차라리 or 아예 often reinforces it. Common in speech and writing alike.

contrasts.note: The same choice from the other side: -(으)ㄹ지언정 marks the hardship accepted, -느니 the option rejected.
-(으)ㄹ망정 also marks the hardship accepted: 굶을망정 구걸은 안 한다 ≈ 구걸하느니 차라리 굶겠다.

examples.ko: 이렇게 줄 서서 한 시간을 기다리느니 차라리 다른 데 가서 먹자.
examples.en: Rather than wait an hour in this line, let's just go eat somewhere else.

examples.ko: 마음에도 없는 말로 위로하느니 아무 말도 안 하는 게 낫다고 생각했다.
examples.en: I thought saying nothing was better than offering comfort I didn't mean.

cloze.sentence: 그 사람한테 부탁을 {{}} 차라리 내가 밤을 새우는 게 낫겠다.
cloze.en: I'd sooner stay up all night than ask him for a favor.

nearMiss.hint: -(으)ㄹ지언정 attaches to the hardship you accept; asking him is the option you reject, so it takes -느니.

cloze.sentence: 그 돈을 주고 그런 집에 {{}} 차라리 좀 멀어도 넓은 데로 가겠다.
cloze.en: I'd rather move somewhere bigger, even if it's farther out, than pay that much to live in a place like that.

nearMiss.hint: 살다 drops its ㄹ before -느니: 사느니.

cloze.sentence: 이렇게 맛없는 걸 {{}} 차라리 굶겠다.
cloze.en: I'd rather go hungry than eat something this bad.

nearMiss.hint: -(으)ㄹ지언정 marks the hardship you accept; eating this is the option you reject, so it takes -느니.

cloze.sentence: 그 사람 잔소리를 {{}} 차라리 혼자 하는 게 낫지.
cloze.en: I'd rather do it alone than listen to him nag.

nearMiss.hint: -(으)니 gives a reason. -느니 attaches straight to the stem: 듣느니.

cloze.sentence: 이걸 처음부터 다시 {{}} 차라리 새로 사는 게 싸겠다.
cloze.en: It'd be cheaper to just buy a new one than make this all over again from scratch.

nearMiss.hint: 만들다 drops its ㄹ before -느니: 만드느니.

cloze.sentence: 정부는 부실기업을 계속 {{}} 차라리 정리하는 편이 낫다고 판단했다.
cloze.en: The government concluded it was better to wind down the insolvent firms than keep propping them up.

cloze.sentence: 이렇게 하루 종일 집에만 {{}} 나가서 산책이라도 하자.
cloze.en: Rather than sit around at home all day like this, let's at least go out for a walk.

cloze.sentence: 억지로 관계를 이어 가며 {{}} 차라리 깨끗하게 헤어지는 게 서로에게 좋아.
cloze.en: Rather than keep seeing each other out of obligation, it's better for both of us to make a clean break.

cloze.sentence: 이 시간에는 택시를 {{}} 차라리 걸어가시는 게 낫습니다.
cloze.en: At this hour, you're better off walking than waiting for a taxi.

nuance.situation: 그 친구 차를 얻어 타면 한 시간 내내 운전 자랑을 들어야 해요. 차라리 걸어가겠다고 말하려면? (Riding with him means an hour of bragging about his driving. You'd rather walk.)

options.text: 그 사람 차를 타느니 차라리 걸어가겠어.
options.why: -느니 marks the rejected option (his car); 차라리 introduces the lesser evil you choose.

options.text: 차라리 걸어가느니 그 사람 차를 타겠어.
options.why: Grammatical, but reversed: it says you'd ride with him rather than walk.

options.text: 그 사람 차를 탈지언정 걸어가겠어.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ지언정 marks the hardship you accept, so this says you'd ride with him and still walk, which doesn't hang together.

nuance.situation: 마음에 드는 코트가 있는데 너무 비싸요. 그 돈을 내고 사느니 안 사겠다고 말하려면? (You love a coat but it's far too expensive. You'd rather not buy it than pay that much.)

options.text: 이 돈 주고 사느니 차라리 안 사고 말지.
options.why: -느니 marks the rejected option (paying that much); the main clause is the lesser evil you choose.

options.text: 이렇게 비싸느니 차라리 안 사고 말지.
options.why: In the "rather than" sense, -느니 attaches to verbs (the option you reject), not to adjectives like 비싸다.

options.text: 이 돈 주고 살지언정 차라리 안 사고 말지.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ지언정 marks the hardship you accept, so it says you'd buy it and also not buy it.
